public_rationale: The Next Web's August 6, 2026 report relayed an estimate that OpenAI supplied around 70% of Microsoft's AI sales [e1]. That estimate covered the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 and used an estimated annual AI revenue total [e1]. It does not measure the January–March 2026 revenue pace used to assess the claim [e1]. The February 27 joint statement confirms Azure's exclusive hosting of stateless OpenAI APIs and continued hosting of OpenAI's first-party products [e2]. It gives no measure of OpenAI's share of Microsoft's infrastructure [e2]. These items leave both the estimated quarterly revenue share and the majority-infrastructure assertion unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: No matching January–March 2026 revenue figures establish the estimated 70% share.
The contract interprets 'its infrastructure' as Microsoft's AI compute infrastructure. The packet supplies no comparable total capacity and OpenAI allocation for that quarter.
The hosting disclosure does not quantify Microsoft's share of OpenAI's overall cloud use or independently establish primary-provider status.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: He estimates that OpenAI represents around 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue while taking up the majority of its infrastructure.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft is OpenAI’s primary cloud provider, and I estimate that OpenAI represents around 70% of its AI revenue, while taking up the majority of its infrastructure.
statement.document_title: Am I Meant To Be Impressed?

from_speaker: Microsoft is OpenAI’s primary cloud provider
taking up the majority of its infrastructure
our_interpretation: Read the revenue estimate as OpenAI's share of Microsoft's current AI revenue pace, consistent with the surrounding run-rate comparisons.
For the ongoing quantitative claims, use January–March 2026, the latest completed Microsoft reporting quarter before the May 6 post.
Read 'its infrastructure' as Microsoft's AI compute infrastructure, given the surrounding discussion of GPUs, rather than all Microsoft infrastructure.
Read 'majority' as more than half of available AI compute capacity allocated to OpenAI workloads, measured consistently across the numerator and denominator.
Treat primary-cloud-provider status as a separate relationship statement; it does not establish either quantitative share.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence for January–March 2026 establishes that OpenAI supplied approximately 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue pace and occupied more than half of its relevant AI compute capacity, with the primary-provider relationship also established.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially contradict the approximate revenue share, establish an infrastructure share of no more than half, or establish that Microsoft was not the primary provider. Any supported and contradicted components must be identified separately.
